questions.q: A coil of inductive reactance $3 1 Ω$ has a resistance of $8 Ω$. It is placed in series with a condenser of capacitive reactance $2 5 Ω$. The combination is connected to an ac source of $\text{110}\text{V}$. The power factor of the circuit is
questions.solution:
${X}_{L} = 3 1 Ω \text{,} {X}_{C} = 2 5 Ω \text{,} \text{R} = 8 Ω$

Impedance of series $LCR$ is

$\text{Z} = \sqrt{\left(R^{2}\right) + {\left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)}^{2}}$

$= \sqrt{{\left(8\right)}^{2} + {\left(3 1 - 2 5\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{6 4 + 3 6} = 1 0 Ω$

Power factor, $\text\cos ϕ = \dfrac{\text{R}}{\text{Z}} = \dfrac{8}{1 0} = \text{0.8}$

questions.q: A solenoid has $\text{2000}$ turns wound over a length of $\text{0}\text{.30 m}$. The area of its cross section is $1.2 \times {10}^{- 3}m^{2}$. Around its central section, a coil of $\text{300}$ turns is wound. If an initial current of $\text{2 A}$ in the solenoid is reversed in $\text{0}\text{.25 s}$, then the emf induced in the coil is equal to
questions.solution:
$Emf = \dfrac{Mdi}{dt} = \left(\dfrac{{μ}_{0} {N}_{1} {N}_{2} A}{l}\right)\dfrac{di}{dt}$
$= \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 2000 \times 300 \times 1.2 \times {10}^{- 3}\left(4\right)}{0.3 \times 0.25}$

$= 4.8 \times {10}^{- 2}$ V

questions.q: The magnetic flux through a circuit of resistance $\text{R}$ changes by an amount $\Delta ϕ$ in a time $\Delta \text{t}$. Then the total quantity of electric charge $\text{Q}$, that passes through any point in the circuit during this $\Delta \text{t}$ time is, represented by
questions.solution:
Induced emf is given by $ε = \dfrac{\Delta ϕ}{\Delta \text{t}}$

Current, $\text{I} = \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\Delta \text{t}} = \dfrac{\Delta ϕ}{\Delta \text{t}} \times \dfrac{1}{\text{R}}$ [where $Q$ is total charge passed in time $\Delta \text{t}$]

$⇒ \text{Q} = \dfrac{\Delta ϕ}{\text{R}}$

questions.q: A square loop $EFGH$ of side $a$, mass $m$ and total resistance $R$ is falling under gravity in a region of transverse non-uniform magnetic field given by $B = {B}_{0}\dfrac{y}{a}$, where ${B}_{0}$ is a positive constant and $y$ is the position of side $EF$ of the loop. If at some instant the speed of the loop is $v$, then the total Lorentz& force acting on the loop is
questions.solution:
Motional emf in EH and FG = 0 as $\overset{\to}{\text{v}} || \overset{\to}{\text{I}}$

Motional emf in EF is ${e}_{1} = \left(\dfrac{{\text{B}}_{0}\text{y}}{\text{a}}\right)\left(\text{a}\right)v ⁡ = {\text{B}}_{0}\text{y}v ⁡$

Similarly, motional emf in GH will be
 
${\text{e}}_{2} = \left\{\dfrac{{\text{B}}_{0}\left(\text{y} + \text{a}\right)}{\text{a}}\right\}\left(\text{a}\right)\left(v ⁡\right) = {\text{B}}_{0}\left(\text{y} + \text{a}\right)v ⁡$
 
Polarities of e1and e2 are shown in adjoining figures.

So the net emf is

$e = {e}_{2} - {e}_{1}e = {B}_{0}av$
$\text{i} = \dfrac{\text{e}}{\text{R}} = \dfrac{{\text{B}}_{0} \text{a} v ⁡}{\text{R}}$ 


${\text{F}}_{\text{EF}} = \left(\dfrac{{\text{B}}_{0} \text{a} v ⁡}{\text{R}}\right) \left(\text{a}\right) \left(\dfrac{{\text{B}}_{0} \text{y}}{\text{a}}\right)$ (downwards)

${\text{F}}_{\text{GH}} = \left(\dfrac{{\text{B}}_{0} \text{a} v ⁡}{\text{R}}\right) \left(\text{a}\right) \left(\dfrac{{\text{B}}_{0} \left(\text{y} + \text{a}\right)}{\text{a}}\right)$ 
 
${\text{F}}_{\text{GH}} = \left(\dfrac{{\text{B}}_{0}^{2}\text{a}v ⁡}{\text{R}}\right)\left(\text{y} + \text{a}\right)$  (upwards)

Net Lorentz force on the loop

${F}_{net} = {\text{F}}_{\text{GH}} - {\text{F}}_{\text{EF}} = \dfrac{{\text{B}}_{0}^{2}{\text{a}}^{2}v ⁡}{\text{R}}$

$F = \dfrac{{B}_{0}^{2}{a}^{2}v}{R}$

questions.q: A superconducting loop of radius $R$ has self-inductance $L$. A uniform and constant magnetic field $B$ is applied perpendicular to the plane of the loop. Initially current in this loop is zero. The loop is rotated by $180 °$. The current in the loop after the rotation is
questions.solution:
Initially, the current was zero, so self-induced flux was also zero. Now when we rotate the loop, the change in flux is

$\Deltaϕ = 2\piR^{2} \times B$

Finally, to maintain the same zero flux, the current in the superconducting loop will be such that the flux due to induced current will negative of the flux due to external field

$L \times i = 2\piR^{2} \times B$.

$i = \dfrac{2\piR^{2} \times B}{L}$

A ring of mass $4kg$ is uniformly charged with a linear charge density $\lambda = 4C{cm}^{- 1}$ and kept on a rough horizontal surface with a friction coefficient of $\mu = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$. A time-varying magnetic field $B = {B}_{0}{t}^{2}$ is applied in a circular region of radius $a \left(a < r\right) perpendicular to the plane of the ring as shown in the figure. Find out the time when the ring just starts to rotate on the surface. (take $a = 5cm$, $g = 10m{s}^{- 2} and {B}_{0} = 125$ SI units)

$
questions.solution:
Induced electric field,
$E ( 2\pi r ) = \dfrac{d \phi}{dt}$
$E = \dfrac{{\pi a}^{2}2{B}_{0}t}{2\pi r}$
Torque due to field about centre of ring,
${τ}_{1} = ( qE ) r = ( \lambda ( 2\pi r ) ) \left(\dfrac{2{\pi a}^{2}{B}_{0}t}{2\pi r}\right)r$
The ring starts rotating when,
$τ$ due to electric field $= τ$ due to friction.
${τ}_{1} = \left(\mu mg\right)r$
Solving,
$t = \dfrac{\mu mg}{2{\pi a}^{2}{B}_{0}\lambda} = 4s$ .

questions.q:
As shown in figure, the two parallel conducting rails, in a horizontal plane, are connected at one end by an inductor of inductance$L$. A slider (metallic) of mass $m$, is imparted a velocity ${v}_{0}_{,} upon the rails, as shown in figure. The period of oscillation of the conducting rod is

$
questions.solution:
From energy conservation (there are no dissipative forces)-

$E = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}LI^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{2} \times 2v\dfrac{dv}{dt} + \dfrac{L}{2} \times 2I\dfrac{dI}{dt} = 0$

$mv\dfrac{dv}{dt} = - IL\dfrac{dI}{dt}$

The emf induced in an inductor is

$E = L\dfrac{dI}{dt} = Blv$

$⇒ L\dfrac{dI}{dt} = Bl\dfrac{dx}{dt} ⇒ LdI = Bldx ⇒ I = \dfrac{Bl}{L}x$

The force acting on a current-carrying conductor is

$m\dfrac{dv}{dt} = - IBl$

$⇒ \dfrac{dv}{dt} = - \dfrac{IBl}{m}$

Substituting the value of $I$ we get

$\dfrac{dv}{dt} = - \left(\dfrac{Bl}{L}x\right)\dfrac{Bl}{m} ⇒ a = - \left(\dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}}{mL}\right)x$

We got acceleration in the form of

$a = - {ω}^{2}x$

this implies that the motion is& SHM, with angular frequency

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}}{mL}}$

The time period of motion is

questions.q: Two long coaxial solenoids of radius $R$ and $2R$ have equal number of turns per unit length. questions.solution:
The magnetic field due to the inner solenoid (within its volume) is

${B}_{1} = {μ}_{0}n \left(2kt\right)$

The magnetic field due to the outer solenoid (within its volume) is

${B}_{2} = {μ}_{0}n \left(kt\right)$

The flux of magnetic field through the circular area of radius $r$ is

$ϕ = {B}_{1}\piR^{2} + {B}_{2}\pir^{2}$

$⇒ ϕ = \pi{μ}_{0}nkt \left(2R^{2} + r^{2}\right)$

If $\overset{→}{E}$ is the induced electric field at $r$, then

$∮ \overset{→}{E}. d\overset{→}{r} = - \dfrac{dϕ}{dt}$

$⇒ E \times2\pir = \pi{μ}_{0}nk \left(2R^{2} + r^{2}\right)$

$⇒ E = {μ}_{0}nk \left(\dfrac{R2}{r} + \dfrac{r}{2}\right)$

The radius of the circle traversed by the charged particle is

$r = \dfrac{mv}{q{B}_{2}}$

$v = E\dfrac{qt}{m} = {μ}_{0}nk\left(\dfrac{R2}{r} + \dfrac{r}{2}\right)\dfrac{qt}{m}$

$⇒ {μ}_{0}nk\left(\dfrac{R2}{r} + \dfrac{r}{2}\right)\dfrac{qt}{m} = \dfrac{qr{B}_{2}}{m}$

$⇒ {μ}_{0}nkt\left(\dfrac{R2}{r} + \dfrac{r}{2}\right) =$ r{μ}_{0}nkt$

$⇒ R^{2} + $\dfrac{r2}{2} =$ r^{2}$

$⇒ r = R\sqrt{2}$

$

Let us assume that the current in the ring is $i$ and the resistance of the two halves are $r$ and $10r$, then by faraday's law

$\left|\dfrac{dϕ}{dt}\right| = \pi{R}^{2}b = ir + i\left(10r\right)$

$⇒ i = \dfrac{\pi{R}^{2}b}{11r}$

The induced electric field in both the parts of the ring is

${E}_{ind} = \dfrac{R}{2}\dfrac{dB}{dt} = \dfrac{Rb}{2}$



Let $E$ be the field which is developed in each part due to charge accumulation at the junctions, then for the upper half

$\left({E}_{ind} + E\right)\piR = i\left(10r\right)$

and for the lower half

$\left({E}_{ind} - E\right)\piR = ir$

$⇒ 2E\piR - 9ir = 0$

$E = \dfrac{9ir}{2\piR}$

$⇒ E = \dfrac{9r}{2\piR} \times \dfrac{\pi{R}^{2}b}{11r} = \dfrac{9}{22}Rb$

$| ε | = \left|\dfrac{dϕ}{dt}\right|$

$= 8volt$

questions.q: There are two solenoids of same length and inductance L but their diameters differ to the extent that one can just fit into the other. questions.solution:
When two solenoids of inductance ${L}_{0}$ are connected in series at large distance and current $i$ is passed through them, the total flux linkage ${ϕ}_{total}$ is the sum of the flux linkages ${L}_{0}i$ and ${L}_{0}i, ie,$

${ϕ}_{total} = {L}_{0}i + {L}_{0}i$

If $L$ be the equivalent inductance of the system, then

${ϕ}_{total} = Li$

$∴ Li = {L}_{0}i + {L}_{0}i$

or $L = 2{L}_{0}$

When solenoids are connected in series with one inside the other and senses of the turns coinciding, then there will be mutual inductance $L$ between them. In this case the resultant induced emf in the coils is the sum of the emf $s{e}_{1}$ and ${e}_{2}$ in the respective coils, $ie,$

$e = {e}_{1} + {e}_{2}$

$= \left(- {L}_{0}\dfrac{di}{dt} \pm {L}_{0}\dfrac{di}{dt}\right) + \left(- {L}_{0}\dfrac{di}{dt} \pm {L}_{0}\dfrac{di}{dt}\right)

Where (+) sign is for positive coupling and (-) sign for negative coupling.

But, $ e = - L . $\dfrac{di}{dt}

$∴ - L$\dfrac{di}{dt} = - {L}_{0}\dfrac{di}{dt} - {L}_{0}\dfrac{di}{dt} \pm2{L}_{0}\dfrac{di}{dt}

$ ie, L = {L}_{0} + {L}_{0} + 2{L}_{0}$

$= 4{L}_{0}$ (for positive coupling)

When solenoids are connected in series with one inside the other with senses of the turns opposite, then their is negative coupling.

So, $L = {L}_{0} + {L}_{2} - 2{L}_{0} = 0

$⇒ m\left({v}_{f} - u\right) = - lBQ - \dfrac{{B}^{2}{l}^{2}}{R}x$

$⇒ Q = \dfrac{- \dfrac{{B}^{2}{l}^{2}}{R}x - m\left({v}_{f} - u\right)}{Bl} = 1C$

questions.q: A long solenoid of the cross-sectional radius $R$ has a thin insulated wire ring tightly put on its winding. One half of the ring has the resistance $10$ times that of the other half. The magnetic induction produced by the solenoid varies with time as $B = bt$, whose b is a constant. If the magnitude of the electric field strength in the ring is $\dfrac{p}{q}Rb$, where $p and q$ are the smallest positive integers, then what is the value of $\left(p + q\right)$?
questions.solution:
Both upper half and lower half will have same effective area of $\dfrac{\pi {R ⁡}^{2}}{2}$ so charge in flux will be same and induced emf will have some value. But since the resistance is different due to which current must be different but ring is as a whole is closed circuit so electric field will be generated to make the current flow in both parts to be same.





$ε + E ⁡ \pi R ⁡ - i ⁡ 1 0 r ⁡ = 0 \ldots \left(i ⁡\right)$

$ε - E ⁡ \pi R ⁡ - i ⁡ r ⁡ = 0 \ldots \left(i ⁡ i ⁡\right)$

$⇒ 2 E \pi R ⁡ - 9 i ⁡ r ⁡ = 0$

$E ⁡ = \dfrac{9 \text{i} \text{r}}{2 \pi R ⁡} ⇒ i ⁡ = \dfrac{E ⁡}{1 1 r ⁡} = \dfrac{\pi {R ⁡}^{2} b}{1 1 r ⁡}$

$⇒ E ⁡ = \dfrac{9 \text{r}}{2 \pi R ⁡} \times \dfrac{\pi {R ⁡}^{2} b}{1 1 r ⁡} = \dfrac{9}{2 2} \text{Rb}$

∴ $\dfrac{9}{2 2} \text{Rb}$
